The `examples/gt_2026` directory preserves the supplied Greenland turbot
projection files. The revised species input contains 47 recruitment values
and 45 SSB values. The helper audits this mismatch and stops staging before
creating an attempt directory. Matching source histories, population body
weights, units, age and plus-group alignment, and SS3 export-field mapping
require confirmation before assessment use. This article executes the audit
and demonstrates the staging block; it generates no projection results.

## Simple commands

Install the current spmR package and work from a clone of the
[source repository](https://github.com/afsc-assessments/spmR). From its root:

```{r}
#| eval: false
source("examples/gt_2026/run.R")
check_gt2026_inputs()
```

The audit reads the current source values. Supply matching recruitment and
SSB histories before staging. `diagnostic = TRUE` selects working population
weights, units and ages explicitly; it cannot supply missing history values.
Once inputs are complete, each successful default staging call creates
`examples/gt_2026/spmR_runs/attempt-###`, retaining source snapshots, SHA-256
hashes, embedded declarations, and staging decisions. Existing attempt
directories are protected against overwriting.

## Audit the supplied files

The following chunks locate and audit the example during an article build.
They require the source checkout or source package, where the example files
are available.

```{r}
#| include: false
if (file.exists(file.path("..", "DESCRIPTION"))) {
  pkgload::load_all("..", export_all = FALSE, helpers = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
} else {
  library(spmR)
}
example_candidates <- c(
  file.path("..", "examples", "gt_2026"),
  file.path("examples", "gt_2026")
)
example_dir <- example_candidates[
  file.exists(file.path(example_candidates, "run.R"))
][1]
if (is.na(example_dir)) {
  stop("Clone the spmR source repository to run this example.")
}
example_dir <- normalizePath(example_dir, mustWork = TRUE)
source(file.path(example_dir, "run.R"), local = TRUE)
```

```{r}
audit <- check_gt2026_inputs(example_dir)
gt::gt(audit)
```

The input now explicitly declares `per sex`. Its two identical recruitment
series contain 47 values each, wrapped across four lines and ending in
`811.8, 460.5`. The SSB series has 45 values, ending in
`28053.3, 27020.6, 25862.1`. The recruitment label still says 1978–2022
and the SSB label says 1978–2026; confirm the numerical histories and their
calendar alignment from the source export. The revised average five-year F
is `0.05605452`, with new female and male abundance vectors over 30 ages.

The helper accepts the wrapped recruitment series and explicit basis. Once
matching source histories are available, it can stage one recruitment copy,
move the basis declaration into the versioned comment block, and replace four
zero spawning weights with `1e-12` for the positive-weight contract. It keeps
Tier 3 historical-recruitment mode (`Rec_Gen = 1`). That mode still requires
matching positional recruitment and SSB lengths.

The obsolete placeholder sidecar was removed from the canonical example;
earlier source snapshots remain archived. Separate JSON and native metadata
files are optional in version 0.4.3: the helper writes
validated declarations as comments in the staged species file. The current
native engine reads those comments directly. `spm.tpl` is self-contained and
requires no separate C++ header.

## Confirm the staging block

The current mismatch is reported as an expected input error, and no attempt
directory is created. An unexpected error still stops the article build.

```{r}
attempt_dir <- tempfile("spmr-gt2026-article-")
staging_status <- tryCatch(
  run_gt2026_projection(
    source_dir = example_dir,
    run_dir = attempt_dir,
    run = FALSE
  ),
  error = function(condition) {
    detail <- conditionMessage(condition)
    if (!grepl("47 recruitment values but 45 SSB values", detail, fixed = TRUE)) {
      stop(condition)
    }
    detail
  }
)
stopifnot(is.character(staging_status), !dir.exists(attempt_dir))
cat("Staging blocked:", staging_status)
```

## Stage complete inputs after review

Diagnostic mode uses `0.96 × fleet 1 + 0.04 × fleet 2` catch-weight proxies
separately for each sex as population weights. These coefficients are the
supplied fishing-mortality allocation. The mixture is a computational assumption
and requires review as a representation of population body weight. Diagnostic
mode also declares thousand fish, kg, tonnes, and ages 1–30 with a terminal
plus group. Whether the supplied spawning weights already incorporate maturity
requires confirmation; the all-one maturity fields are neutral multipliers. Under those fields,
`Ntot` and `SexRatio` describe all fish and the all-fish female fraction.

```{r}
#| eval: false
staged <- run_gt2026_projection(
  source_dir = example_dir,
  run_dir = tempfile("spmr-gt2026-article-"),
  diagnostic = TRUE,
  run = FALSE
)
staged$run_dir
```

This command is displayed without execution. It requires matching source
histories and an explicit decision to use the diagnostic assumptions.

## Run an explicitly chosen diagnostic projection

After supplying matching histories and reviewing the assumptions, these commands enable native execution.
They are displayed without execution in this article.

```{r}
#| eval: false
gt2026 <- run_gt2026_projection(diagnostic = TRUE)
gt2026$summary
gt2026$run_dir
```

The helper uses `admb` on `PATH`, `SPMR_ADMB`, or its `admb` argument to compile
the installed template. `SPMR_CXX` selects a matching C++ compiler. A compatible
existing executable can be selected with `SPMR_EXECUTABLE` or `executable`.
If compilation still requests `spmr_input_v2.hpp`, reinstall spmR from the
current checkout and restart R to refresh the installed template.

A completed run under the supplied controls would contain 105,000 detail rows: seven alternatives, 1,000
simulations, and 15 projection years (2026–2040). The helper verifies the row
keys, finite outputs, initial biomass, fixed catches, and successful provenance.
Gradient and Hessian fit diagnostics are inapplicable to historical-recruitment
simulation. These checks establish the conditional calculation; the SS3 export
definitions and scientific interpretation require their own review.

## Replace the population-weight assumptions

Provide actual female and male population body-weight vectors with verified
units and age labels:

```{r}
#| eval: false
gt2026 <- run_gt2026_projection(
  population_weights = list(
    female = female_body_weights,
    male = male_body_weights
  ),
  units = verified_units,
  ages = verified_ages
)
```

Each vector must align with the 30 supplied age positions. Confirm the
beginning-of-2026 abundance state, plus group, and recruitment/SSB year pairing
against the SS3 export code and source fields. Supplying population weights
alone leaves those remaining checks open. The example README contains the
complete input evaluation and terminal commands.
